evidence.quote: an Actor Recently Tied to Ryuk and LockerGoga Ransomware

data.context: Recently, FireEye Managed Defense detected and responded to a FIN6 intrusion at a customer within the engineering industry, which seemed out of character due to FIN6's historical targeting of payment card data.

evidence.quote: FIN6's historical targeting of payment card data

data.context: This blog post details the latest FIN6 tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), including ties to the use of LockerGoga and Ryuk ransomware families.

evidence.quote: ties to the use of LockerGoga and Ryuk ransomware families

data.context: The subsequent investigation revealed FIN6 was in the initial phase of an intrusion using stolen credentials, Cobalt Strike, Metasploit, and publicly available tools such as Ad fi nd and 7-Zip to conduct internal reconnaissance, compress data, and aid their overall mission.

evidence.quote: using stolen credentials, Cobalt Strike

data.context: Managed Defense investigated activity on two systems initially detected as compromised by FireEye Endpoint Security, the industry leading endpoint security solution that was ranked as the most e ff ective endpoint detection and response (EDR) solution.

evidence.quote: the industry leading endpoint security solution

data.context: Managed Defense utilized Windows Registry Shellbag entries to reconstruct FIN6's actions on compromised systems that were consistent with lateral movement.

evidence.quote: reconstruct FIN6's actions on compromised systems

data.context: Following the compromise of this system, analysts identi fi ed FIN6 leveraged stolen credentials to move laterally within the environment using the Windows' Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).

evidence.quote: using the Windows' Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP)

data.context: Following the RDP connection to systems, FIN6 used two di ff erent techniques to establish a foothold: First technique: FIN6 used PowerShell to execute an encoded command.

evidence.quote: FIN6 used PowerShell

data.context: Figure 1: Base64 encoded command The encoded payload was a Cobalt Strike h tt psstager that was injected into the PowerShell process that ran the command.

evidence.quote: Cobalt Strike h tt psstager

data.context: The Cobalt Strike h tt psstager was con fi gured to download a second payload from hxxps://176.126.85[.]207:443/7sJh.

evidence.quote: download a second payload

data.context: FireEye retrieved this resource and determined it was a shellcode payload con fi gured to download a third payload from hxxps://176.126.85[.]207/ca.

evidence.quote: FireEye retrieved this resource and determined it was a shellcode payload

data.context: The investigations observed FIN6 using similar tools, tactics, and procedures that were observed by FireEye Managed Defense during the earlier phases of the a tt ack lifecycle.

evidence.quote: using similar tools, tactics, and procedures

data.context: Lateral Movement FIN6 used encoded PowerShell commands to install Cobalt Strike on compromised systems.

evidence.quote: Lateral Movement FIN6 used encoded PowerShell commands

data.context: The a tt acker made use of Cobalt Strike's 'psexec' lateral movement command to create a Windows service named with a random 16-character string on the target system and execute encoded PowerShell.

evidence.quote: The a tt acker made use of Cobalt Strike's 'psexec'

data.context: In some cases, the encoded PowerShell commands were used to download and execute content hosted on the paste site hxxps://pastebin[.]com.

evidence.quote: the encoded PowerShell commands were used to download and execute content

data.context: The distribution servers were used to stage the LockerGoga ransomware, additional utilities, and deployment scripts to automate installation of the ransomware.

evidence.quote: stage the LockerGoga ransomware

data.context: FIN6 automated the deployment of kill.bat and the LockerGoga ransomware using batch script fi les.

evidence.quote: automated the deployment of kill.bat and the LockerGoga ransomware using batch script fi les

data.context: Figure 2: Strings from deployment BAT fi les start copy svchost.exe \\10.1.1.1\c$\windows\temp\start psexec.exe \\10.1.1.1 -u domain\domainadmin -p "pass Ransomware Ryuk is a ransomware that uses a combination of public and symmetric-key cryptography to encrypt fi les on the host computer.

evidence.quote: Strings from deployment BAT fi les

data.context: LockerGoga is ransomware that uses 1024-bit RSA and 128-bit AES encryption to encrypt fi les and leaves ransom notes in the root directory and shared desktop directory.

evidence.quote: uses 1024-bit RSA and 128-bit AES encryption

data.context: Additional information about Ryuk and LockerGoga is available on the FireEye Intelligence po rt al: 1800015730 and 19-00002005 Attribution FIN6 has traditionally conducted intrusions targeting payment card data from Point-of-Sale (POS) or eCommerce systems.

evidence.quote: Additional information about Ryuk and LockerGoga is available on the FireEye Intelligence po rt al: 1800015730 and 19-00002005

data.context: However, we have recently identi fi ed multiple targeted Ryuk and LockerGoga ransomware incidents showing ties to FIN6, through both Mandiant incident response investigations and FireEye Intelligence research into threats impacting other organizations.

evidence.quote: identi fi ed multiple targeted Ryuk and LockerGoga ransomware incidents

data.context: We have traced these intrusions back to July 2018, and they have repo rt edly cost victims tens of millions of dollars.

evidence.quote: We have traced these intrusions back to July 2018, and they have reportedly cost victims tens of millions of dollars.

data.context: As the frequency of these intrusions deploying ransomware have increased, the cadence of activity traditionally a tt ributed to FIN6-intrusions targeting point-of-sale (POS) environments, deploying TRINITY malware and sharing other key characteristics-has declined.

evidence.quote: targeting point-of-sale (POS) environments

data.context: Given that these intrusions have been sustained for almost a year, we expect that continued research into fu rt her intrusion a tt empts may enable us to more fully answer these questions regarding FIN6's current status.

evidence.quote: further intrusion attempts
